pages.text: A scalar field φ with potential V = ½m²φ² inflates while it rolls slowly: the slow-roll parameter ε = 2/φ² (in reduced Planck units) must stay below 1, and the number of e-folds N = (φ₀² − 2)/4 must reach about 60 to make a smooth, flat universe. Start too high, though, and quantum jumps of the field outrun its classical roll - inflation becomes eternal and the bubble never reheats.
$(thing)Set$(): Initial field φ₀, Reheating coupling Γ.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Quantum fluctuations kick the starting field by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): No inflation: the field is too low on its potential (ε above 1); Too few e-folds: the bubble comes out curved and lumpy; Eternal inflation: quantum jumps outrun the roll and the bubble never reheats; Reheating too weak: the universe stays cold and empty; The containment sphere is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More e-folds and a hotter reheating make the work go faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective field: φ = φ₀·(1 + 0.03·d)$(br)Slow-roll ε: ε = 2/φ²$(br)e-folds N: N = (φ₀² − 2)/4$(br)Reheating temperature: T_rh = (90/π²g*)^¼·√(Γ·M_P)
